crop.notes: The main headline 'For the America's Cup' and the first deck lines are cut off at the top; the crop begins mid-deck at '...Made him Conceited—To-Day's Entries and Selections.' The letter runs to its 'Quarter-Stretch' signature. Allen is named once, in the Goddard paragraph.

ocr.notes: Body text mostly right; first line of the transcript is garbage from the cut-off deck.

title.suggested: New York Letter Likens Joe Goddard's Old-Style Fighting to Tom Allen's

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Republic's New York sporting letter said Joe Goddard, conceited after beating Peter Maher, was "no more of a prize fighter in the modern sense of the word than Tom Allen is," all arms and legs in the ring.

metadata.notes: Masthead reads The Republic: St. Louis, Mo., Monday Morning, December 19, 1892, page 5; letter dated New York, Dec. 18, 1892.

notes: Allen appears only as a byword for old-fashioned prize fighting; the title's current wording ('Not a Prize Fighter Like Tom Allen') reverses the comparison. No biographical facts to extract.
